title: A multi‐level approach for multi‐objective optimization in process eco‐design
content:
Abstract

This work addresses a central challenge in process eco-design: how to efficiently integrate environmental and economic criteria—often conflicting—into early design stages while managing the high dimensionality of Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) indicators. To this end, we propose a generic six-level multi-objective methodology combining process simulation, LCA, a modified NSGA-II genetic algorithm, and multiple criteria decision-making (MCDM) models (ELECTRE, PROMETHEE, M-TOPSIS). The approach is applied to the hydrodealkylation of toluene (HDA) for benzene production. Starting from a set of five criteria (four environmental end-points and economic performance), later expanded to 14 environmental mid-points, the method identifies redundant indicators and reduces the optimization to the most influential objectives. Results show that a bi-objective optimization (economic performance vs. human-health impacts) is sufficient to represent trade-offs previously captured by the full 14-indicator space. Quantitatively, the optimized solutions achieve 12%–18% reductions in environmental end-point impacts relative to single-objective economic optimization, without increasing operating costs. Mid-point results indicate that ozone layer depletion is the dominant contributor among human-health categories, guiding the formulation of a refined optimization problem. MCDM techniques consistently identify similar compromise solutions, confirming the robustness of the reduced-criteria strategy. Overall, this framework demonstrates that combining LCA, multi-objective optimization, and MCDM into a structured multi-level workflow enables engineers to reduce problem complexity while achieving environmentally improved designs that remain economically viable.
